about.title: Montague Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Montague is a small community, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when someone gets hurt on a broken step, icy sidewalk, or unmarked spill. Whether the fall happened at a business along 11th Th St, a rental property near Ager Road, or a public building elsewhere in town, California law requires the owner to show they either knew about the hazard or reasonably should have and failed to address it. That's the heart of a premises liability claim here. Because Montague is rural and many properties see less foot traffic, evidence like surveillance footage, maintenance logs, or witness accounts can disappear quickly. Acting early to document the scene and preserve any video matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law, but we can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who understands how these claims work under California's notice and comparative-fault rules, and who takes cases on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California law asks whether the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network can help gather the evidence needed to answer that question in your favor.

items.title: Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage and maintenance records are often overwritten or discarded within days. Connecting with an attorney quickly can help preserve what's needed before it's lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to End Your Claim
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you share some fault for the fall, though it may reduce your compensation. An independent attorney can help present your side clearly under this pure comparative fault rule.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Montague?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a personal injury lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, that window is much shorter and requires an earlier claim filing. Speaking with an attorney soon after the incident helps make sure important deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover damages even if you were partially responsible, though your compensation may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This applies whether the fall happened at a shop off Big Springs Road or elsewhere in Siskiyou County. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Are slip and fall claims different in a small town like Montague?
items.answer: The legal standard is the same statewide, but rural areas can raise practical challenges, like fewer surveillance cameras or witnesses at smaller businesses along corridors such as N 11th Street. That makes it even more important to document the scene, take photos, and gather names of anyone nearby right after the fall. An independent attorney can guide you on what evidence to collect given the specific property involved.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we're not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
